correctness.rationale: The Beta moments E Y²=1/(2a+1), E Y⁴=3/((2a+1)(2a+3)) yield variance 4a/((2a+1)^2(2a+3)) and exactly reproduce 1,y,y² with the normalized symmetric kernel. Rescaling z=sqrt(2a+1)y gives K=1+sqrt(2a+1)xz+((2a+3)/(4a))((2a+1)x²-1)(z²-1). Uniform finite moments imply Lambda_a(x)/a -> 4phi(1)x²; the uniform differentiated sign limit on [delta,1] and a strict gap on |x|<=1/2 show only +/-1 maximize for sufficiently large real a. The central x=z/sqrt(2a+1) Hermite limit is locally uniform. At x=1 the exact kernel is a(z²-1)+sqrt(2a+1)z+(3z²-1)/2, and weighted standardized-beta expansion phi(z)(1-H4(z)/(8a))+o(a^-1) plus moving-simple-root expansion at +/-1 gives Gaussian parts (6phi(1)+4Q-1)+2phi(1)-phi(1)=7phi(1)+4Q-1. Independent exact-rational beta reproduction and 55-digit numerical integration confirm component identities and limiting errors at seven a values; finite checks do not prove any infinite statement.

value.rationale: The quadratic continuous Jacobi/Gegenbauer orthogonal projector is a canonical approximation operator. The exact first two coefficients of its large-weight sharp L1/Linfinity norm measure endpoint amplification and norm instability in high concentration, while its central Gaussian scaled profile stays bounded. The uniform spatial law and eventual uniqueness of the two endpoint worst evaluations supply a meaningful structural location result. These exact invariants are not a mere known-table restatement or trivial normalization of a polynomial moment; researchers investigating endpoint least-squares stability, Jacobi parameters and Hermite crossover can use both coefficients and location behavior. The familiar Gaussian limit alone would not meet this claim of value.
residual_risks: No higher-degree or asymmetric Jacobi theory follows from this fixed-degree proof.
A future user would still need quantitative a0 and finite-a phase behavior.

final_claim: For a>0, mu_a(dy) proportional to (1-y^2)^(a-1)dy on [-1,1] and P_a the exact continuous L2(mu_a) projector onto span{1,y,y²}, as a->infinity at fixed degree two, both L1 and Linfinity endpoint norms equal 4phi(1)a+7phi(1)+4Q-1+o(1) with Q=Pr(Z>1), and the only pointwise Lebesgue-function maximizers for every sufficiently large real a are x=+/-1. Uniformly for x in [-1,1], Lambda_a(x)/a -> 4phi(1)x². At x=z/sqrt(2a+1), the profile tends locally uniformly to E|1+zZ+(z²-1)(Z²-1)/2|.
limitations: Only degree two, large a; no explicit unique-maximizer threshold a0, no small-a phase diagram or higher-degree extension.
